newsitem.title: USA: Calif. endorses bill to prohibit Internet taxation.
newsitem.headline: Calif. endorses bill to prohibit Internet taxation.

text.p: California's governor Monday endorsed federal legislation that would place a national moratorium on taxing Internet transactions.
The Internet Tax Freedom Act, authored by Rep. Chris Cox, a California Republican, would prevent state and local governments from imposing new taxes on Internet transactions.

Internet-related companies are growing at a rapid pace in California. The state could be hard hit if the Internet becomes a major tax collection target, Republican Gov. Pete Wilson said in a statement.
"This bill will ensure that the Internet industry will have a chance to develop without the market distortions caused by a haphazard tax structure," Wilson said.
California is the first state in the nation to support the legislation, which faces its first hearing Thursday in the Senate Commerce Committee, Wilson said.

Earlier this year the California Board of Equalization, the state's tax collection agency, voted unanimously in support of the legislation, along with several state taxpayer groups, including the Silicon Valley Software Alliance.
In March, Cox said he wanted to prevent the World Wide Web from becoming the "World Wide Wallet" for governments looking for additional tax revenues.
Sales of goods and commerce on-line are projected to grow to over $7 billion in the year 2000 from less than $1 billion last year, according to market researchers at Jupiter Communications.
